title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Trademark Dispute Cases

articles.content_en: Article 2: Pursuant to the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 13 of the Trademark Law, where a person reproduces, imitates, or translates another person's well-known trademark not registered in China or its principal part and uses it as a trademark in respect of identical or similar goods, which is likely to cause confusion, that person shall bear the civil liability for ceasing the infringement.

Article 4: The interested parties provided in Paragraph 1 of Article 60 of the Trademark Law include the licensee under a contract for the use license of a registered trademark, the legal successor to the property right in a registered trademark, and others.
Where the exclusive right to use a registered trademark is infringed, the licensee under an exclusive use license contract may institute an action with the People's Court; the licensee under a sole use license contract may institute an action jointly with the trademark registrant, or may institute an action on its own where the trademark registrant does not institute an action; the licensee under an ordinary use license contract may institute an action upon explicit authorization by the trademark registrant.

Article 5: Where a trademark registrant or an interested party files an application for renewal of a registered trademark within the grace period for renewal, and before the renewal is approved, institutes an action on the ground that another person has infringed its exclusive right to use the registered trademark, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Article 6: A civil action instituted because of an act of infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court of the place where the infringing act as provided in Articles 13 and 57 of the Trademark Law is committed, the place where the infringing goods are stored, the place where the infringing goods are sealed up or detained, or the place of the domicile of the defendant.
The place where infringing goods are stored as provided in the preceding paragraph refers to the place where a large quantity of infringing goods or infringing goods are stored or concealed on a regular basis; the place of sealing up or detention refers to the place where infringing goods are sealed up or detained according to law by administrative authorities such as the customs.

Article 7: For a joint action brought against multiple defendants involving different places where the infringing acts are committed, the plaintiff may select, for jurisdiction, the People's Court of the place where the infringing act of one of the defendants is committed; for an action brought only against one of the defendants, the People's Court of the place where that defendant's infringing act is committed shall have jurisdiction.

Article 8: The relevant public as mentioned in the Trademark Law refers to consumers related to a certain class of goods or services identified by a trademark and other business operators having a close relationship with the marketing of the aforesaid goods or services.

Article 9: The identical trademark as provided in Items (1) and (2) of Article 57 of the Trademark Law means that, as compared with the plaintiff's registered trademark, the accused infringing trademark has essentially no visual difference.
The similar trademark as provided in Item (2) of Article 57 of the Trademark Law means that, as compared with the plaintiff's registered trademark, the shape, pronunciation, or meaning of its characters, or the composition and color of its design, or the overall structure after combination of its elements are similar, or its three-dimensional shape or color combination is similar, which is likely to cause the relevant public to misidentify the source of the goods or to believe that there is a specific connection between the source and the goods of the plaintiff's registered trademark.

Article 11: The similar goods as provided in Item (2) of Article 57 of the Trademark Law refer to goods that are identical in aspects such as function, use, production department, sales channel, and target consumers, or goods that the relevant public generally considers to have a specific connection and that are likely to cause confusion.
Similar services refer to services that are identical in aspects such as purpose, content, manner, and target, or services that the relevant public generally considers to have a specific connection and that are likely to cause confusion.
Similarity between goods and services means that there is a specific connection between the goods and the services, which is likely to cause confusion among the relevant public.

Article 12: When the People's Court determines, pursuant to the provisions of Item (2) of Article 57 of the Trademark Law, whether goods or services are similar, it shall make a comprehensive judgment based on the general understanding of the relevant public with respect to the goods or services; the International Classification of Goods and Services for the Purposes of the Registration of Marks and the Classification Table of Similar Goods and Services may be used as references for determining similar goods or services.

Article 13: When the People's Court determines the liability for damages of the infringer pursuant to the provisions of Paragraph 1 of Article 63 of the Trademark Law, it may calculate the amount of damages according to the calculation method chosen by the right holder.

Article 14: The profits obtained from the infringement as provided in Paragraph 1 of Article 63 of the Trademark Law may be calculated on the basis of the product of the volume of sales of the infringing goods and the unit profit of such goods; where the unit profit of such goods cannot be ascertained, the calculation shall be made on the basis of the unit profit of the goods bearing the registered trademark.

Article 15: The losses suffered from the infringement as provided in Paragraph 1 of Article 63 of the Trademark Law may be calculated on the basis of the reduction in the sales volume of the goods caused by the infringement to the right holder, or the product of the sales volume of the infringing goods and the unit profit of the goods bearing the registered trademark.

Article 16: Where the actual losses suffered by the right holder as a result of the infringement, the profits obtained by the infringer from the infringement, and the fee for the trademark use license are all difficult to determine, the People's Court may, upon the request of a party or ex officio, apply the provisions of Paragraph 3 of Article 63 of the Trademark Law to determine the amount of damages.
When the People's Court applies the provisions of Paragraph 3 of Article 63 of the Trademark Law to determine the amount of damages, it shall take into consideration such factors as the nature, duration, and consequences of the infringement, the degree of subjective fault of the infringer, the reputation of the trademark, and the reasonable expenses incurred in stopping the infringing act, and determine the amount comprehensively.
Where the parties reach an agreement on the amount of damages pursuant to the provisions of Paragraph 1 of this Article, such agreement shall be permitted.

Article 17: The reasonable expenses paid for stopping the infringing act as provided in Paragraph 1 of Article 63 of the Trademark Law include the reasonable expenses incurred by the right holder or the authorized agent in investigating and obtaining evidence of the infringing act.
The People's Court may, according to the litigation claims of the parties and the specific circumstances of the case, include in the scope of damages the attorney's fees that conform to the provisions of the relevant State authorities.

Article 18: The limitation of action for infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark shall be three years, calculated from the date on which the trademark registrant or the interested right holder knows or should have known of the damage to the right and of the obligor. Where the trademark registrant or interested party institutes an action after more than three years, if the infringing act is still ongoing at the time the action is instituted and the exclusive right to use the registered trademark is still within its valid term, the People's Court shall adjudge that the defendant cease the infringing act, and the amount of damages for infringement shall be calculated retroactively for three years from the date on which the right holder institutes the action with the People's Court.
Article 19: The failure to record a trademark use license contract shall not affect the validity of the license contract, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

Article 20: The assignment of a registered trademark shall not affect the validity of a trademark use license contract that has already taken effect before the assignment, unless otherwise provided in the trademark use license contract.

Article 21: In trying a dispute case involving infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark, the People's Court may, pursuant to the provisions of Article 179 of the Civil Code and Article 60 of the Trademark Law and in light of the specific circumstances of the case, adjudge that the infringer bear civil liability such as ceasing the infringement, removing the obstruction, eliminating the danger, compensating for losses, and eliminating the adverse effects, and may also make a decision on civil sanctions such as imposing a fine and confiscating the infringing goods, forged trademark labels, and materials, tools, equipment, and other property mainly used for producing the infringing goods. The amount of the fine may be determined by reference to the relevant provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 60 of the Trademark Law.
Where the administrative department has already imposed an administrative penalty on the same act of infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark, the People's Court shall not impose civil sanctions again.

Article 22: In trying trademark dispute cases, the People's Court may, according to the request of the parties and the specific circumstances of the case, make a determination according to law as to whether the registered trademark involved is a well-known trademark.
The determination of a well-known trademark shall be made in accordance with the provisions of Article 14 of the Trademark Law.
Where a party requests protection for a well-known trademark that has previously been determined by an administrative authority or the People's Court, and the opposing party does not object to the well-known status of the trademark involved, the People's Court shall not review it again. If the opposing party raises an objection, the People's Court shall review it in accordance with the provisions of Article 14 of the Trademark Law.
Article 23: The provisions of this Interpretation concerning goods trademarks shall apply to service trademarks.
Article 24: Where any previous relevant provisions are inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
